title: WW/WC Reset to Default
context: Greenfield WPF/MVVM feature for CT image display: adds a Reset Window/Level button that restores DICOM-default WW (0028,1051) and WC (0028,1050) values. IEC 62304 Class B. The infrastructure task (1 of 4 = 25%) exceeds the 20% guideline because no ExtInf/ or Src/ tree exists yet — all interface contracts, the WindowLevel value object, and DICOM constants must be established before any vertical feature slice can build on them. File counts per task also exceed the 2–5 guideline due to greenfield creation (new files, not modifications).

tasks.title: Infrastructure: Domain model, interface contracts, and DICOM constants

Scenario: Zero Window Width is rejected

Scenario: WindowLevel preserves the DICOM preset name
Scenario: DICOM display tag constants map to correct tag numbers
tasks.design_note: See ADR-001 §Architectural Envelope for the ExtInf interface contracts (IImageDisplayViewModel, IDicomImageModel, IStatusNotifier, IUndoService, IUndoableAction, IWindowLevelDefaults), the WindowLevel value object with WW > 0 invariant enforced by WindowLevel.Create(), and DicomDisplayTags constants referencing DICOM PS3.3 §C.7.6.3.1.5. File: .harness/architecture/adr/ADR-001-ww-wc-reset-design.md

tasks.design_note: See ADR-001 §Decision item 3: IWindowLevelDefaults configuration service reads fallback WW=400, WC=40 from application settings (configurable without rebuild per FR-04). §Decision item 6: WindowLevel.Create() rejects WW ≤ 0 at construction time (FR-07). Command logic: if IDicomImageModel.DefaultWindowLevel is null or WW ≤ 0 → use IWindowLevelDefaults.FallbackWindowLevel → log WARNING → notify user with distinct message.
